newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down for third straight session.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down for third straight session.

text.p: * Main index closes 24.91 pts down, 0.73 pct, at 3,371.13
The Philippine stock market closed in negative territory in light trade on Thursday as the Chinese New Year celebrations kept investors at bay, traders said.

"Most of the orders are on the sell side and those taking the limelight are the smaller issues. Its really the absence of players that's dragging the market," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity.
"There was really no panic selling. The market is strong and what happened was accumulation on certain issues," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital.
Value turnover was light at 2.7 billion pesos compared to the recent four to five billion pesos worth of shares traded daily.
Decliners beat gainers 75 to 53 with 76 issues unchanged.
Of the blue-chips, Petron Corp suffered much selling pressure and ended 50 centavos lower, or 4.35 percent, at 11 pesos in heavy volume at 3.775 million shares.

"With the implementation of full deregulation just days away investors may be seeing some volatility in that sector so that they opted for the way out and we saw selling in Petron,: said Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities.
Ferrer added the continued absence of players on Friday would restrict trading activity.
